description: Bicep storage account whose network rules default to Allow
note: CIS Azure 4.7 and 4.8. Bicep now has two sources, not one. KICS parses .bicep natively where Trivy has no Bicep scanner at all, so this case's self-check compares two tools and the single-source caveat multi-iac-spec §4 carried for Bicep is retired. This case previously expected one rule where its ARM twin expected three, because 4.8 was reachable only through Trivy and Trivy has no Bicep scanner. KICS covers 4.8 on both, so the asymmetry is gone. CORRECTED after the confirming run: KICS's Trusted Microsoft Services query was expected here for the 4.8 half and does not fire, for exactly the reason checkov's CKV_AZURE_36 does not -- an explicit defaultAction of Allow suppresses it in both. Measured 2026-09-23 across the four combinations: no networkAcls at all FIRES, defaultAction Allow is SILENT, Deny without the bypass FIRES, Deny with AzureServices is SILENT. So the precondition is not 'Deny is required' -- an absent block fires too -- it is that an explicit Allow switches the check off. Which is defensible: bypass is a carve-out from a block, and if everything is allowed there is no block to carve out of. Two independent tools agreeing makes it the rule rather than a quirk of one. 4.8 is exercised by the insecure-transfer cases instead, where the account declares no networkAcls at all.
